clue.text: Worthless people finally put in cellar

parts.note: base means low, of little worth
men means people

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word put

parts.note: last letter of put

explanation.surface: Good-for-nothings are locked away in the cellar at last.
explanation.definitionFit: A basement is the storey below ground level of a house, the same thing as a cellar.

clue.text: Press for admission to surgery

indicators.note: the answer is admitted inside the word surgery, sitting within its letters

explanation.surface: Someone pushes to be let into a doctor's surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: To press someone is to urge them, a verb synonym meaning to push hard for something.

clue.text: One working the land is used to steer

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a person who tills soil, a farmer
second meaning: the bar fixed to a boat's rudder for steering

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition has an implied 'something which' before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A farmer who cultivates soil tills it, and a boat's rudder is turned with a lever of the same name.

clue.text: After starters of tapas, very delightful private meal on lap?

indicators.note: starters are the opening letters, here of tapas, very and delightful

parts.note: inner means private, personal and hidden

explanation.surface: Following some tapas nibbles, a lovely intimate meal is held on someone's knees.
explanation.definitionFit: A ready meal eaten in front of the television is often balanced on the knees, hence the question mark.

clue.text: To annoy old flame eat pears messily

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: messily says the letters of eat pears are jumbled

explanation.surface: Irritating a former lover by eating pears in a slovenly way.
explanation.definitionFit: To exasperate someone is to irritate them intensely, a strong synonym.

clue.text: Starts to run over many classic old movies, this sort typical?

definitions.text: Starts to run over many classic old movies, this sort typical?

indicators.note: starts are the first letters of each of the following six words

explanation.surface: A film buff's scan through a stack of old classic films.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue doubles as a description: classic old movies of this kind are a typical sort of film.
explanation.definitionFit: A romcom is a romantic comedy, a familiar staple film genre.

clue.text: Initially high flyers sort of crack

indicators.note: initially gives the first letter of the word high

parts.note: first letter of high
an airline is a company whose planes carry flyers

explanation.surface: High-flying travellers are, from the start, a cracking kind of thing.
explanation.walkthrough: Flyers is read loosely: an airline is what flies people about.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairline crack is a very thin fracture, as fine as a strand of hair.

clue.text: Pass bottom of slope and slip

indicators.note: in a down entry the bottom of a word is its last letter, here of slope

parts.note: last letter of slope
a lapse is a slip or minor error

explanation.surface: Someone passes the foot of a slope and loses their footing.
explanation.definitionFit: Time is said to elapse when it passes or slips by.

clue.text: After victory sign, steer dad into street interview

indicators.note: after says the following pieces come behind the victory sign

parts.note: V is the two-finger victory sign
a steer is a castrated bull, an ox
pop is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: Someone flashing a V sign drives their father into an interview on the street.
explanation.definitionFit: A vox pop, Latin for voice of the people, is a broadcast of passers-by giving their opinions.

clue.text: Used to be poor at the last with little around

indicators.note: around says the word for little encloses the letter

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small

indicators.note: at the last picks the final letter of poor

parts.note: last letter of poor

explanation.surface: A sketch of someone who was once poor at the end, with a little around them.
explanation.definitionFit: Were is a past tense form of the verb to be, so it means existed in the past.

clue.text: Master of camouflage worried, if scent found on meadow

indicators.note: found on places the anagram next to the meadow, coming after it

parts.note: lea is a poetic word for a meadow

indicators.note: worried, meaning agitated, says the letters of if scent are shaken up

explanation.surface: A nervous creature in a meadow because it caught a scent.
explanation.definitionFit: This insect looks so much like a leaf that predators overlook it, a supreme camouflage artist.

clue.text: More loved, even if up in price

definitions.meaning: first meaning: comparative of dear, cherished

explanation.definitionFit: Dear means both beloved and costly, so its comparative covers greater affection and a higher cost.

clue.text: In rehearsal hurry from beginning to end

parts.note: to run is to hurry
through means from start to finish, as in all the way through

explanation.surface: Racing through a play's practice from start to finish.
explanation.definitionFit: A run-through is a practice performance of a show or speech, done straight through.

clue.text: Star smiles in bright lights

parts.note: the sun is a star
to beam is to smile broadly, so beams are smiles

explanation.surface: A celebrity grins under the glare of bright lights.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunbeams are rays of sunshine, shafts of brilliant light.

clue.text: Avoid being involved in support

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to watch without intervening
second meaning: to remain loyal to them

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb has opposite-feeling senses: idly watching on, or loyally backing a friend.

clue.text: Beast about to grab a girl — not fair

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for beast surrounds the other piece

parts.note: a brute is a savage beast
to net is to catch or grab

explanation.surface: A monster closes in to seize a young woman, which is hardly fair play.
explanation.definitionFit: A brunette is a woman with dark brown hair, the opposite of a blonde or fair-haired one.

clue.text: Wave going right through vessel

indicators.note: through says the right letter passes inside the word for a vessel

parts.note: a beaker is a drinking or laboratory vessel

explanation.surface: A wave that crashes right through a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a boat but is a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A breaker is a heavy sea wave that crests and smashes onto the shore.

clue.text: Think I'm trespassing in someone's grounds

indicators.note: trespassing in means going inside someone else's land, so these letters enter it

parts.note: an estate is the land around a large house
I'm without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to thinking they are trespassing on private land.
explanation.definitionFit: To estimate is to reckon or judge roughly, so in this sense it means to think.

clue.text: Give a wrong idea of felon's first conviction

parts.note: to belie is to misrepresent or give a false impression of

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of felon's

parts.note: first letter of felon's

explanation.surface: A misleading account of a criminal's first time being found guilty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conviction' wants to be legal, but here it means a firmly held view.
explanation.definitionFit: A belief is a firmly held opinion, which is the sense of conviction used here.

clue.text: In super-busy environment had failed to feed little animal

indicators.note: to feed means to go into, so the jumbled letters are put inside the animal

parts.note: a mouse is a small animal

indicators.note: failed says the letters of had have broken down and are reordered

explanation.surface: In a chaotic setting someone forgot to feed the pet mouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failed' looks like part of the story about forgetting to feed the pet, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A madhouse is informally any chaotic, frantically busy place, like an asylum in uproar.

clue.text: Language of associate academician and writer

parts.note: ARA stands for Associate of the Royal Academy
a Bic is a brand of ballpoint pen

explanation.surface: The language spoken by an associate member of an academy and a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' is a pen, not an author.
explanation.definitionFit: Arabic is the Semitic tongue spoken across the Middle East and North Africa.

clue.text: Cover small moor

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
a heath is open uncultivated land, a moor

explanation.definitionFit: A sheath is a close-fitting covering or case, such as one for a blade.

clue.text: English railways directed up past it

indicators.note: in a down entry, directed up means the letters run bottom to top, so reversed

parts.note: lines are railway routes

explanation.surface: English trains sent up the line long after their prime.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone past it is too old to function well, which is what senile describes, an idiom for decrepit.

clue.text: Have an iron prepared for old George

indicators.note: prepared means made ready, so the letters of have an iron are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone is told to get an iron ready for the old king.
explanation.definitionFit: Kings George I to IV belonged to the royal house of Hanover, so each was a Hanoverian monarch.

clue.text: Heard some pressure in drain

indicators.note: heard says a word that sounds like some is spelled differently

parts.note: some is said aloud, sounding like sum
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Somebody hears some pressure building up in the drains.
explanation.definitionFit: A sump is a pit or well where waste liquid collects, so it acts as a drain.

clue.text: Pouches in which commandos keep cape

indicators.note: keep means to hold within, so the commandos contain the cape letter

parts.note: SAS is the Special Air Service, the British army's special forces regiment
C is the map abbreviation for cape

explanation.surface: Soldiers stash a cape in their kit pouches.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacs are small baglike cavities in animals or plants, natural pouches.

clue.text: Not very bright, about to father baby

indicators.note: about signals turning round the word for not very bright

parts.note: dim means dull or not clever
get in the archaic sense of beget, to father a child

explanation.surface: A dullard is about to become a father.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' reads as 'soon to', but 'about' reverses the word for not very bright and 'to father' gives GET. Both answer and definition act as adjectives meaning small.
explanation.definitionFit: As adjectives, baby and midget both describe something tiny, as in a baby or miniature version.

clue.text: Happiness in life, moving to big place

indicators.note: moving means stirring around, so the letters of life are rearranged

parts.note: a city is a large town

explanation.surface: Finding joy by relocating to the big city.
explanation.definitionFit: Felicity is a formal word for great happiness or bliss.
